Testimony for the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs in support of LD 2017 An Act to Update Certain Statutes Governing School Nutrition as amended
January 21, 2026
Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy, and esteemed members of the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs, I'm Anna Korsen, Deputy Director with Full Plates Full Potential, a statewide non-profit working to address childhood food insecurity in Maine by maximizing access to federally funded USDA nutrition programs like school meals and the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). We are a founding member of the Hunger Free Maine Coalition who advocates to advance the priorities of Maine's Roadmap to End Hunger. I also serve as the co-chair of the Ending Hunger in Maine Advisory Committee and Full Plates is a contracted SNAP Outreach organization with the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS).
I am testifying in support of LD 2017 as amended, as this bill fixes two existing child nutrition policies in Maine to reflect currently available data and streamline program administration.
The first part of the bill proposes to amend existing language that requires the Maine Department of Education (DOE) to contract with an outside entity to provide an online application for eligibility in school meals. Our understanding is that the intent behind this change is to streamline the application process for schools and families by combining the school meal application with an existing application that families use to qualify for other benefits. We fully support this effort and intent, and this type of initiative is a key priority in Maine's Roadmap to End Hunger.1
The second part of the bill proposes to strike language that measures participation in school breakfast among children eligible for free and reduced price school meals. The data required for that measurement is no longer readily available due to the fact that many schools now participate in the Community Eligibility Provision, and are unable to track participation in school breakfast and lunch by eligibility category. Maine schools continue to have high participation rates in school breakfast among all students, and last school year over 60,000 students participated in school breakfast daily.2
Please support LD 2017. Thank you for your time- I am happy to answer any questions.
Anna Korsen akorsen@fullplates.org 207-653-6301

Testimony of Jane McLucas, Director of Child Nutrition, Maine Department of Education

In Support of: L.D. 2017
An Act to Update Certain Statutes Governing School Nutrition

Before the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs

Sponsored by: Representative Murphy

Date: January 21, 2026

Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy, and Members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Education and Cultural Affairs:

My name is Jane McLucas, and I am here today representing the Department speaking in support
of L.D. 2017 An Act to Update Certain Statutes Governing School Nutrition. This bill seeks to

update certain sections of the Maine School Lunch statutes in order to align with recent program
changes. First, LD 2017 removes the requirement that the Maine Department of Education (DOE)

contract for an internet-based application for free or reduced-price school meals and instead simply

allows the Department to take that action. It also removes the burdensome requirement that a public

school is solely responsible for processing that school's online applications. Second, the bill
removes an exemption related to altemative breakfast delivery service which we no longer have

the data for.

_

In many cases, these changes are required as a result of the Governor's successful no-charge meals in Maine and seek to further reduce the stigma of school meal debt and further ensure student
access to nutritious food. An added benefit of LD 2017 is that it reduces the administrative burden
on our school administrative units (SAUs). By allowing flexibility in the provision of the online free and reduced-price meal application, SAUs will be empowered to make a choice that suits their
needs.

The Department would like to offer a friendly amendment to the bill. We suggest leaving 20-A

Chapter 223 subchapter 11 intact.

_

Department of Education is in support of L.D. 2017. I am happy to answer any questions the Committee may have, and I will be available for work sessions on this bill.

Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs: I am Representative Kelly Murphy, and today I am here to introduce a bill for the Department of
Education, LD 2017, An Act to Update Certain Statutes Governing School Nutrition.
This bill updates several areas of statute that have been rendered obsolete due to changes in the
way the State of Maine administers free and reduced-price breakfast and lunch at school. The Department will offer a friendly amendment, which will preserve statutory language related to
food access and discipline.
The Department of Education will present testimony on this bill, and I respectfully request that you defer any specific questions regarding the content to them. I look forward to working with you as the committee deliberates the bill.
Thank you for your consideration of this bill.

TESTIMONY IN SUPPORT OF
L.D. 2017
AN ACT TO UPDATE CERTAIN STATUTES GOVERNING SCHOOL NUTRITION
Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy, and members of the Education and Cultural Affairs Committee, I am Robbie Feinberg, Director of Communications and Government Relations for Maine School Management Association, testifying on behalf of the legislative committees of the Maine School Boards Association and Maine School Superintendents Association in support of L.D. 2017.
School leaders across Maine have seen the immense impact that Maine's universal school meals program has had on student behavior, learning and well-being, and we are thankful for the legislature and your committee for continuing to support this effort.
One consequence of that legislation has been ensuring an accurate count of students in each district who are economically disadvantaged. This number directly impacts the amount of funding that our state receives from the federal government for meal reimbursement, and also has an impact on the amount of state and federal funding that each school district ultimately receives.
Districts had previously used free-and-reduced-price lunch counts to determine these student numbers. But the change to universal school meals has made it more difficult to get an accurate FRPL count. We have supported the state's recent efforts to utilize direct certification, instead of relying on parents to fill out forms from their school, and we believe L.D. 2017 could improve that process even further.
From our conversations with the department, L.D. 2017 will help to facilitate the development of an online portal that will allow Maine families to complete applications for free and reduced-price meal forms while they complete other benefit forms, such as when applying for MaineCare or SNAP benefits.
We believe this is a common sense approach - allowing state agencies to assist our local districts in accounting for these families, streamlining the meal application process, and ensuring Maine and local districts receive federal and state dollars they need to best educate their students.
School meals are crucial to the health and well-being of Maine children. L.D. 2017 will further streamline the meal application process and reduce administrative burdens, and we urge your committee to support it.
Thank you for your consideration.

Eric F. Waddell
MSBA Executive Director

Eileen E. King
MSSA Executive Director
